title: CDC says to offer common allergy foods when other solids start, one new food at a time
summary: CDC says eggs, shellfish, nut butters, and wheat can be introduced with other foods, with a few days between new foods.
body: The CDC solids page, dated 14 April 2026, says to let a child try one single-ingredient food at a time at first, so a caregiver can see problems such as food allergies, and to wait 3 to 5 days between each new food. It also says to introduce potentially allergenic foods when other foods are introduced. The examples are eggs, shellfish, nut butters, and wheat. If a child has severe eczema or an egg allergy, the page says to talk with a doctor or nurse about when and how to introduce peanut foods safely. This is United States feeding guidance. It is not a diagnosis, and it does not list rescue steps for a severe reaction.

sources.title: When, What, and How to Introduce Solid Foods
sources.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.note: Supports the one-food and allergenic-food sentences. Public-domain CDC page. Paraphrased. No treatment steps.
